verdicts.evidence: The piece at L2 bbox (5.70..8.22, -10.85..-7.34), 0.72 m2, is the only Level 2 wall piece with no cut fill (0 % fill). verdicts.how: General parapet rule in build_model.py: an unfilled wall piece (under 25 % fill) whose ends meet railings at two places at least 0.5 m apart is part of the balustrade. It becomes kind 'parapet' at railingHeight 1.10 m with follow=false, on layer BB_L2_Parapets. The test checks the top is 1.10 with nothing above; the negative control (parapet at 3.70) fails that check.

verdicts.evidence: There are 11 (L1) and 5 (L2) 'Basic Wall _ GLASS WALL 2600H 20X100' blocks on A-WALL. Each holds only 1-4 face lines. Their 10 mm A-WALL fills are top-level and lie within 10 cm of the block lines: 14 panes on L1 (8.6 m) and 5 on L2 (8.4 m). All were built as 3.70 m wall. Doors L1-005/007/008/022 and L2-010 had opaque lintels. L1-027 stands between two 10 mm screens.
verdicts.how: General Revit-export rule (documented in the README and the docstring). A block on a wall layer is a wall element, read by its type name. GLASS / GLAZED / GLAZING / CURTAIN makes it glass, and '<n>H' gives its height (2600H = 2.60 m). Its panes are the thin fills (3 cm or less) within 10 cm of its lines, plus any joined to them. Their bands, widened to the type faces, are removed from the wall. The result is 19 glass panes, 0-2.60 m, follow=false, each its own Max object named after the type. There is 1 corner frame post. Doors whose jambs are both glass get glass transoms to the lower glass top: 5 to 2.60 m, and L1-027 to 3.70 m. Thin fills at the jambs of a door whose name says GLASS are frameless screens (2, full height). Tests: the partitions stop you and stand to 2.60 m with nothing above; the doors show a transom at their head. The negative control fails.

verdicts.evidence: The facade wall ends face each other at y 7.619 and 8.201: a 0.58 m gap at x 6.13-6.24, with no detected opening. The hull of the 'ATM Machine - ATM Machine-V26' block covers it and reaches out of both faces. A gap search over all wall ends on both levels finds only this gap with an object in it. The other 0.58 m gap, on L2 at (0.42..1.0, 11.45..11.6), has no object and is left.
verdicts.how: General rule: two wall ends facing each other along one line, at most 1.2 m apart and of the same thickness, with no opening between them and an object block in the gap that reaches out of both faces, get closed. The object block must sit on a layer that builds nothing and hold no building items, which excludes the Revit link block. The closure is a full-height wall part, BB_L1_Wall_010_closure (ATM Machine ...). The test checks it stands to 3.70 m; removing it fails the test.

verdicts.evidence: The L2 slab was one polygon with no holes. Every S-STRS line was a 0.15 m fin, and the lift shaft had floor on L2. The L2 drawing carries the words UP (4.68, 9.52) and DOWN (4.68, 7.65) at the flights' east ends, and its A-FLOR floor-edge line runs at x 4.55.
verdicts.how: On levels above the first there is now no floor over each stair outline (the hull of its lines, 9.3 m2) or over a lift shaft (3.1 m2). A lift shaft is a room whose only opening is a door whose block name says LIFT/ELEVATOR. Flights are found as 3+ parallel riser lines 0.19-0.37 m apart, sorted into lanes; a riser hidden by the break line is put back. A stair word at a flight's end gives its direction, and the flight becomes solid steps one riser apart (riser = floor height / ceil(H/0.18) = 0.176 m). That gives 16 steps on L2. Flights without a word (all of L1's) are drawn as flat 3 cm tread strips instead of fins. On L2, stair lines and 3 stair rails over no floor are left out. Tests: no floor over the 2 stairs and the lift shaft on L2; the steps sit one riser apart. Both fail in the negative control. Owner question: the L1 and L2 stair drawings do not line up.

verdicts.evidence: The old L2 plate reached y 12.71 over the north stair, which has 18 risers and no door. The L1 plate had a bulge at its foot.
verdicts.how: New plate rule. The plate is the inside of walls, glass and openings, where every detected opening spans its gap. A railing-bounded area from the 1.5 m closing is added only if it has standing room (0.8 m), a detected door or passage opens onto it, and it is not mostly stair. The terrace is kept (52.7 m2). Dropped: 4.67 m2 on L2 and 1.26 m2 on L1, both 'mostly stair'. Covered by the test's no-floor-over-stairs check (the north stair point is off the L2 floor).
